_: THIS GATE AIMED AT ITS OWN SUITE — run it from the harness's directory:
Every property this gate holds is a property its suite claims to hold, and a
claim nobody has broken is a claim nobody has measured. Each injection here
removes ONE of them and names the tests that must go red. A green run says
the suite is not vacuous; a `did not reach` says a test passes for a reason
other than the one it is written for.
Keep it runnable: the `from` texts are exact, and a source edit that moves
one of them makes this sweep refuse out loud rather than pass quietly.

injections.name: an-unreached-target-counts-as-clean
injections.why: the whole reason this gate exists is that `found nothing wrong` and `never opened it` print the same; with the unreached arm folded into the clean one, a target rustdoc could not document passes

injections.name: the-second-authority-is-never-asked
injections.why: rustdoc cannot see a #[test] item, so without the harness's list every citation naming a sibling test is convicted and the `a law citing the law next to it` idiom becomes a wall of defects

injections.name: the-second-authority-excuses-everything
injections.why: the other direction, and the one that empties the gate: excusing a name the harness does NOT list turns a stale test citation into a pass

injections.name: a-test-target-is-not-handed-its-own-crate
injections.why: cargo passes a test target's documentation unit an extern for every dependency and none for the crate under test; without the repair, every test that uses its own crate is unreachable

injections.name: the-extern-is-handed-to-targets-cargo-already-wired
injections.why: a binary already receives its package's library, and a second extern for it is E0464 and documents nothing — the failure that came back as three unreached binaries

injections.name: test-targets-leave-the-population
injections.why: this is the shape of the gate it replaces: `cargo doc` documents no test target at all, so a citation in one is not wrong, it is unasked

injections.name: a-bench-target-is-not-handed-its-dev-dependencies
injections.why: a bench target receives NEITHER its own crate nor its dev-dependencies; with only the first put back, criterion still resolves to nothing and rustdoc documents the target not at all

injections.name: a-dependency-in-both-tables-is-treated-as-dev-only
injections.why: a crate named in [dependencies] AND [dev-dependencies] is already passed by cargo; adding it again is E0464, and the census is the only thing that keeps it out

injections.name: a-run-cargo-never-finished-is-treated-as-finished
injections.why: the ARM-B trap this round met in its own measurement: rustdoc refused a flag, reported zero citations and exited non-zero, and counting citations alone said clean
